Imagine…
in a single day, every ocean on Earth drains away.
Almost three quarters of the planet becomes dry land.
You are standing on a beach boulevard.
Normally, the tide moves the water a few meters.
Now, it drops almost eight meters every minute.
The waves fall silent.
After one hour, the sea is more than four hundred meters lower.
People stop.
Lifeguards wave everyone off the beach.
Boats lie on their sides in the mud.
The oceans hold about one point three billion cubic kilometers of water.
On average, they are about three point seven kilometers deep.
But the sea was doing much more than holding water.
It soaked up most of the extra heat in our climate.
Its plankton made around half of the oxygen produced on Earth.
By the end of the day, the last water runs into the Mariana Trench.
Almost eleven kilometers down.
Then, the wind blows salt across the empty sea floor.
Most of the rain on Earth begins as water rising from the sea.
Without it, the sky above you would slowly run dry.
